interest: This document is of historical interest as an archival index record evidencing Japanese cultural diplomacy and educational outreach toward Latin America prior to or during the Second World War. Specifically, it documents Japan's initiative to grant competitive scholarships to students across the five Central American republics, shedding light on Japanese soft power and cultural relations in the Western Hemisphere—a region traditionally viewed as within the United States' sphere of influence.
overview: This file consists of a single-page Department of State 'List of Papers' (docket/index sheet) for decimal file 894.42710, concerning cultural relations between Japan and Latin America, specifically focusing on the exchange of professors and students and the attendance of American students at schools in Japan. The sheet indexes an entry for Sub No. 1, noting a communication dated December 10 from McKinney regarding ten scholarships in Japan to be awarded on a competitive basis to two students from each of the five Central American republics, along with a reference to Japanese currency.
